### Eagle Bancorp Montana Earns $3.0 Million, or $0.38 per Diluted Share, in the Third Quarter of 2026, Declares Quarterly Cash Dividend of $0.1475 Per Share


October 27, 2026


HELENA, Mont., Oct. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Eagle Bancorp Montana, Inc. (NASDAQ: EBMT), (the “Company,” “Eagle”), the holding company of Opportunity Bank of Montana (the “Bank”), today reported net income of $3.0 million, or $0.38 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $3.7 million, or $0.47 per diluted share, in the preceding quarter, and $3.6 million, or $0.46 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2025. In the first nine months of 2026, net income increased to $10.7 million, or $1.36 per diluted share, compared to $10.1 million, or $1.29 per diluted share, in the first nine months of 2025.


Eagle’s board of directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.1475 per share on October 22, 2026. The dividend will be payable on December 4, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 13, 2026. The current dividend represents an annualized yield of 2.58% based on the average closing price of the Company’s common stock reported on NASDAQ during the third quarter of 2026 of $22.91 per share.


“Our third quarter was defined by record loan growth and continued strength in our core deposit franchise,” said Laura F. Clark, CEO. “Total loans increased $159.0 million from the prior quarter, with growth across our markets and lending lines that reflects strong customer demand and the deep relationships our bankers have built. Importantly, we grew without compromising our credit discipline or pricing. Net interest margin remained solid at 4.12%, and the larger loan portfolio we built this quarter positions us to grow earnings in the periods ahead. With a strong core deposit base supporting this growth, we enter the final quarter of the year with positive momentum and remain focused on delivering long-term value for our shareholders.”


**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights** (at or for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, except where noted):


- Net income was $3.0 million, or $0.38 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $3.7 million, or $0.47 per diluted share in the preceding quarter, and $3.6 million, or $0.46 per diluted share, in the third quarter a year ago.
- Net interest margin (“NIM”) was 4.12% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 4.15% in the preceding quarter and 3.94% in the third quarter a year ago.
- Net interest income, before the provision for credit losses, increased 4.4% to $20.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $19.1 million in the second quarter of 2026, and increased 7.0% compared to $18.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.
- Revenues (net interest income before the provision for credit losses, plus noninterest income) were $25.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $24.2 million in the preceding quarter and $23.4 million in the third quarter a year ago.
- Total loans of $1.72 billion increased $159.0 million compared to June 30, 2026, and increased $159.6 million compared to a year earlier.
- Due to the record loan growth, Eagle recorded a $1.9 million provision for credit losses for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a $343,000 provision for credit losses in the preceding quarter and a $62,000 provision for credit losses in the third quarter a year ago. Borrower specific deterioration did not meaningfully affect the provision for credit losses for the third quarter of 2026.
- The allowance for credit losses was $19.5 million, or 1.13% of total loans, at September 30, 2026, compared to $17.6 million, or 1.13% of total loans, at June 30, 2026, and $17.7 million, or 1.14% of total loans, a year ago.
- Total deposits of $1.80 billion increased $11.9 million compared to June 30, 2026, and increased $49.9 million, or 2.8%, compared to a year earlier.
- Eagles’s common shareholders’ equity (book value) per share was $24.12 at September 30, 2026, compared to $24.78 at June 30, 2026, and $23.45 at September 30, 2025. Tangible book value per share (non-GAAP) was $19.44 at September 30, 2026, compared to $20.07 at June 30, 2026, and $18.63 at September 30, 2025.
- The Company’s available borrowing capacity was approximately $452.2 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $575.0 million at June 30, 2026, and $508.4 million at September 30, 2025. Short-term FHLB advances were utilized in the quarter to support loan production.
- The Company paid a quarterly cash dividend in the third quarter of $0.1475 per share on September 4, 2026, to shareholders of record August 14, 2026.


**Balance Sheet Results**


Total assets of $2.28 billion at September 30, 2026, increased $162.2 million compared to one year ago, and increased $156.2 million compared to three months earlier. The investment securities portfolio totaled $272.8 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $279.9 million a year ago, and $285.7 million at June 30, 2026.


Eagle originated $80.8 million in new residential mortgage loans during the quarter and sold $74.7 million in residential mortgage loans, with an average gross margin on sale of mortgage loans of approximately 2.70%. This production compares to residential mortgage loans originations of $88.1 million in the preceding quarter with sales of $72.5 million and an average gross margin on sale of mortgage loans of approximately 3.07%.


Total loans increased $159.6 million compared to a year ago and increased $159.0 million compared to three months earlier. Commercial real estate loans increased 17.0% to $784.7 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $670.4 million a year earlier. Commercial real estate loans were comprised of 66.8% non-owner occupied and 33.2% owner occupied at September 30, 2026. Agricultural and farmland loans increased 0.9% to $316.9 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $314.1 million a year earlier. Residential mortgage loans decreased 5.4% to $141.0 million, compared to $149.1 million a year earlier. Commercial loans increased 22.4% to $175.0 million, compared to $143.0 million a year ago. Commercial construction and development loans decreased 7.8% to $104.6 million, compared to $113.5 million a year ago. Home equity loans increased 8.7% to $115.9 million, residential construction loans increased 64.3% to $58.2 million, and consumer loans decreased 17.5% to $21.1 million, compared to a year ago.


Total deposits increased to $1.80 billion at September 30, 2026, from $1.75 billion at September 30, 2025, and $1.79 billion at June 30, 2026. Noninterest-bearing checking accounts represented 25.2%, interest-bearing checking accounts represented 11.5%, savings accounts represented 11.6%, money market accounts comprised 25.9% and time certificates of deposit made up 25.8% of the total deposit portfolio at September 30, 2026. The average cost of total deposits was 1.44% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 1.49% in the preceding quarter and 1.63% in the third quarter of 2025. The estimated amount of uninsured deposits was approximately $369.3 million, or 20% of total deposits including accrued interest, at September 30, 2026, compared to $359.8 million, or 20% of total deposits including accrued interest, at June 30, 2026.


FHLB advances and other borrowings increased to $196.8 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $79.2 million at September 30, 2025, and $52.1 million at June 30, 2026. The average cost of FHLB advances and other borrowings was 4.36% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 5.30% in the preceding quarter and 4.57% in the third quarter of 2025. Other borrowings at September 30, 2026 include the Company’s line of credit draw for $13.0 million at an average rate of 6.37% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $13.0 million at an average rate of 6.34% for the second quarter of 2026.


Shareholders’ equity was $192.1 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $186.5 million a year earlier and $197.4 million three months earlier. The reduction in shareholders’ equity during the third quarter of 2026 was due to an increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss, net of tax on securities available-for-sale. The decrease in fair value of securities was primarily a result of increased interest rates. Book value per share was $24.12 at September 30, 2026, compared to $23.45 a year earlier, and $24.78 three months earlier. Tangible book value per share, a non-GAAP financial measure calculated by dividing shareholders’ equity, less goodwill and core deposit intangible, by common shares outstanding, was $19.44 at September 30, 2026, compared to $18.63 a year earlier and $20.07 three months earlier.


**Operating Results**


“Our net interest margin contracted three-basis points from the prior quarter but was up 18-basis points over the same period a year ago. Compared with last year, the drop in funding costs more than offset a modest decline in earning asset yields, while funding costs held relatively steady from the prior quarter. Looking ahead, we will continue to focus on loan and deposit pricing as we work to protect our net interest margin in a rising rate environment,” said Spaulding.


Eagle’s NIM was 4.12% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 4.15% in the preceding quarter and 3.94% in the third quarter a year ago. The interest accretion on acquired loans totaled $173,000 and resulted in a three-basis point increase in the NIM during the third quarter of 2026, compared to $94,000 and a two-basis point increase in the NIM during the preceding quarter. The average yield on interest earning assets held steady at 5.77% in the third quarter of 2026, matching the prior quarter, compared to 5.87% in the third quarter a year ago. Funding costs for the third quarter of 2026 increased to 2.14%, compared to 2.12% in the second quarter of 2026 and decreased compared to 2.45% in the third quarter of 2025. For the first nine months of 2026, NIM expanded 27-basis points to 4.13% compared to 3.86% for the first nine months of 2025.


Net interest income, before the provision for credit losses, increased 4.4% to $20.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $19.1 million in the second quarter of 2026, and increased 7.0% compared to $18.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. Year-to-date, net interest income increased 7.6% to $57.8 million, compared to $53.7 million in the same period one year earlier.


Revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were $25.1 million, a 3.8% increase compared to $24.2 million in the preceding quarter and a 7.2% increase compared to $23.4 million in the third quarter a year ago. In the first nine months of 2026, revenues were $72.8 million, an 8.2% increase compared to $67.3 million in the first nine months of 2025.


Total noninterest income was $5.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $5.0 million in the preceding quarter, and increased 8.1% compared to $4.7 million in the third quarter a year ago. In the first nine months of 2026, noninterest income increased 10.7% to $15.0 million, compared to $13.5 million in the first nine months of 2025. Net mortgage banking income, the largest component of noninterest income, totaled $2.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, consistent with both the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter a year ago. Net mortgage banking income increased 3.5% to $8.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, compared to $8.0 million in the first nine months of 2025.


“We continue to invest strategically in our team and technology to support long-term growth, while maintaining a disciplined approach to managing expenses,” said Darryl Rensmon, President and Chief Operating Officer. Eagle’s third quarter noninterest expense was $19.4 million, compared to $19.0 million in the preceding quarter, and $18.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. In the first nine months of 2026, noninterest expense increased 6.1% to $56.6 million, compared to $53.3 million in the first nine months of 2025. The increases to the quarterly and year-to-date noninterest expense relate primarily to increases in salaries and employee benefits.


For the third quarter of 2026, the Company recorded income tax expense of $831,000, compared to $1.1 million in the preceding quarter and $1.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. The effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 21.6%, compared to 22.9% for the second quarter of 2026 and 26.8% for the third quarter of 2025. The year-to-date effective tax rate was 22.1% for 2026 compared to 21.1% for the same period in 2025.


**Credit Quality**


Eagle recorded a $1.9 million provision for credit losses for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a $343,000 provision for credit losses in the preceding quarter and a $62,000 provision for credit losses in the third quarter a year ago. The allowance for credit losses represented 224.0% of nonperforming loans at September 30, 2026, compared to 423.5% three months earlier and 430.4% a year earlier. Nonperforming loans were $8.7 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $4.2 million at June 30, 2026, and $4.1 million at September 30, 2025. The increase in nonperforming loans was primarily due to well collateralized agricultural loans. Net loan charge-offs totaled $29,000 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $193,000 in the preceding quarter and $72,000 in the third quarter a year ago. The allowance for credit losses was $19.5 million, or 1.13% of total loans, at September 30, 2026, compared to $17.6 million, or 1.13% of total loans, at June 30, 2026, and $17.7 million, or 1.14% of total loans a year ago.


**Capital Management**


Eagle’s ratio of tangible common shareholders’ equity (shareholders’ equity, less goodwill and core deposit intangible) to tangible assets (total assets, less goodwill and core deposit intangible) was 6.90% at September 30, 2026, compared to 7.12% a year ago and 7.66% three months earlier. This ratio is a non-GAAP financial measure. For the most comparable GAAP financial measure, see “Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below. The Bank’s Tier 1 capital to adjusted total average assets was 10.62% as of September 30, 2026. As of September 30, 2026, the Bank’s regulatory capital was in excess of all applicable regulatory requirements and is deemed well capitalized.


**About the Company**


Eagle Bancorp Montana, Inc. is a bank holding company headquartered in Helena, Montana, and is the holding company of Opportunity Bank of Montana, a community bank established in 1922 that serves consumers and small businesses in Montana through 30 banking offices. Additional information is available on the Bank’s website at[www.opportunitybank.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=hhN-DPbHIo8IZbvj_yZas1vATJZtRxYHbY31jQHGI7HtKgClu_HLOFoxsu-c7u0XVmotvHtmNwXGnbsJln_sCT_fAfQNMTkQu0XU2x6klDSkTVhhb7626jOHOwQnXrF-) . The shares of Eagle Bancorp Montana, Inc. are traded on the NASDAQ Global Market under the symbol “EBMT.”

**Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


In addition to results presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles utilized in the United States, or GAAP, this release, including the Additional Financial Information contains non-GAAP financial measures. Non-GAAP financial measures in this release include: 1) core efficiency ratio, 2) tangible book value per share and 3) tangible common shareholders’ equity to tangible assets. The Company uses these non-GAAP financial measures to provide meaningful supplemental information regarding the Company’s operational performance, performance trends and financial condition, and to enhance investors’ overall understanding of such financial performance. In particular, the use of tangible book value per share and tangible common equity to tangible assets is prevalent among banking regulators, investors and analysts.


The numerator for the core efficiency ratio is calculated by subtracting intangible asset amortization from noninterest expense. Tangible assets and tangible common shareholders’ equity are calculated by excluding intangible assets from assets and shareholders’ equity, respectively. For these financial measures, our intangible assets consist of goodwill and core deposit intangible. Tangible book value per share is calculated by dividing tangible common shareholders’ equity by the number of common shares outstanding. We believe that this measure is consistent with the capital treatment by our bank regulatory agencies, which exclude intangible assets from the calculation of risk-based capital ratios and present this measure to facilitate the comparison of the quality and composition of our capital over time and in comparison, to our competitors.


Non-GAAP financial measures have inherent limitations, are not required to be uniformly applied, and are not audited. Because non-GAAP financial measures are not standardized, it may not be possible to compare these financial measures with other companies’ non-GAAP financial measures having the same or similar names. Further, the non-GAAP financial measure of tangible book value per share should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for book value per share or total shareholders’ equity determined in accordance with GAAP, and may not be comparable to a similarly titled measure reported by other companies. Eagle strongly encourages investors to review its consolidated financial statements in their entirety and not to rely on any single financial measure.
